claims.claim: Catalytic converters were introduced on most US gasoline vehicles starting with the 1975 model year, driven by EPA emissions regulation.
claims.episode_span: For the first generation of catalytic converters introduced in the mid-1970s, automakers and suppliers largely copied the existing pellet-bed or early honeycomb designs already used in industrial pollution-control units.
claims.supporting_quote: stricter regulation of exhaust emissions, most gasoline-powered vehicles starting with the 1975 model year are equipped with catalytic converters

claims.claim: A catalytic converter contains only a few grams of platinum-group metals (roughly 3-7 grams of platinum in a typical unit, per this source).
claims.episode_span: What drives most of the cost is a thin washcoat containing only a few grams of platinum-group metals whose market prices swing sharply with mine output and industrial demand.
claims.source_title: Here's How Much Platinum Is Actually Inside Your Catalytic Converter - Jalopnik
claims.supporting_quote: each catalytic converter only contains roughly 3 to 7 grams of platinum

claims.claim: Ceria and ceria-zirconia oxides are added to catalytic-converter washcoats mainly as oxygen storage promoters.
claims.episode_span: A second move replaced simple alumina supports with stabilized ceria-zirconia mixed oxides that store and release oxygen
claims.supporting_quote: Ceria or ceria-zirconia . These oxides are mainly added as oxygen storage promoters.

claims.claim: Substrate cell densities rose over time: 200-600 cpsi (400 most common) in 1990s gasoline cars, with increasingly higher densities introduced since, in excess of 1000 cpsi.
claims.episode_span: increase the geometric surface area of the cordierite honeycomb by moving from 300 to 400, then 600, and eventually 900 cells per square inch while thinning the walls
claims.source_title: Cellular Monolith Substrates - DieselNet Technology Guide
claims.supporting_quote: Parts that were commercially used for internal combustion engine applications in the 1990s had cell densities between 200 and 600 cpsi, with 400 cpsi being the most common cell density in gasoline car applications. Since then, increasingly higher cell densities have been introduced in gasoline cars

claims.claim: The ceramic substrate used in most catalytic converters is cordierite, invented at Corning Glass.
claims.episode_span: increase the geometric surface area of the cordierite honeycomb
claims.supporting_quote: The cordierite ceramic substrate used in most catalytic converters was invented by Rodney Bagley , Irwin Lachman , and Ronald Lewis at Corning Glass

claims.claim: Rhodium's price is highly volatile, ranging from under US$700 per troy ounce in 2016 to nearly US$30,000 in 2021 - far above platinum's level in those years, supporting the order-of-magnitude comparison.
claims.episode_span: Because rhodium prices can exceed those of platinum by an order of magnitude
claims.supporting_quote: The price of rhodium (per troy ounce) is highly variable, ranging from less than US$700.00 in 2016 to nearly US$30,000.00 in 2021.

claims.claim: Annual world production of rhodium fluctuates around 30 tonnes, i.e., tens of tons per year, mostly from South Africa.
claims.episode_span: annual mine production of rhodium is measured in tens of tons
claims.supporting_quote: Principal production is located in South Africa, at 75%, with much less production in Russia and Zimbabwe. The annual world production flucuates around 30 tonnes

claims.claim: Catalytic converters are a target for thieves because of their external location and the valuable platinum, palladium, and rhodium they contain.
claims.episode_span: whose theft later became attractive precisely because the metals retained high scrap value
claims.supporting_quote: Because of the external location and the use of valuable precious metals including platinum , palladium and rhodium , catalytic converters are a target for thieves.
